why: The CDR primitive readers (`rclc_cdr_read_u8` .. `_f64`), each taking the `(cursor, end, origin)` triple and advancing the cursor. In ROS 2 the CDR encoder belongs to the MIDDLEWARE, not the client library: `rosidl` generates a `rosidl_message_type_support_t` whose function table is filled in by whichever rmw implementation is loaded (FastCDR inside rmw_fastrtps, the ddsi stream writers inside rmw_cyclonedds), and the only byte-level verbs rcl/rclcpp expose are `rmw_serialize`/`rmw_deserialize` on a whole message. No cursor, no per-primitive call, nothing to correlate against. nano-ros has no middleware plugin to hide an encoder inside -- `nros generate-c` emits the `_serialize`/`_deserialize` body into the USER's translation unit and that TU links against libnano_ros -- so the primitives have to be exported symbols. The RTOS constraint that earns it is the one `c:message_type_t` already records: one linked backend, no runtime typesupport registry to dispatch through. The RTOS scenario is the generated message code itself: a `_deserialize` body compiled into a Zephyr or FreeRTOS image, decoding into fixed-size `heapless`-equivalent C storage with no allocator and no stream object -- `origin` exists because CDR alignment is relative to the payload start, and the caller owns the buffer. Recorded honestly rather than as a blanket `extension`: this is CODEGEN MACHINERY published in the user's namespace with nothing marking it so. `cdr_read_string` and the DHEADER verbs are argued on their own rows. Kept where it is by phase-506 W1 (RFC-0071 D12): it already sits behind `nros::internals` / `nros::embedded` or is a C seam, outside the top-level Rust user API D12 is about.
